page: Microsoft Azure F2 is an x86_64 server belonging to the F family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and a bundled local storage capacity of 33 GB. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance.

Performance benchmarks place the F2 instance consistently in the lower tier of modern cloud servers. Both single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, rank in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 14.41 GB/sec and write speeds at 10.79 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 10% category. The server demonstrates weak performance in Passmark CPU extended instructions and small-model LLM inference tasks, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but older Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 architecture, the F2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated execution threads rather than shared-core burstable resources. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and poor overall benchmark results represent a significant tradeoff. This server is best suited for lightweight utility tasks, basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, and simple background processing jobs that do not demand high memory or intensive computational throughput.
